note: Re-judged 2026-10-30 (independent judge, part-B backfill review) after the row's annotation moved from {not-applicable} to {gap: gap in proof}. Draft Section 4, second condition: 'if the interface address of the router through which the announced network is reachable for the speaker is the internal peer's address, the next hop MUST include its own Link- Local IPv6 address.' The obligation binds Ze as a BGP speaker announcing to an internal peer, so not-applicable no longer stands: the earlier verdict rested on an unevidenced exclusion that the ratchet now refuses. Read both producers: internal/component/bgp/reactor/forward_next_hop.go::egressNextHopIsPeerOwn compares the (possibly modified) relayed next hop to the peer's address and withholds the route, and originatedNextHopIsPeerOwn reads the built UPDATE body at the write boundary (Session.writeUpdateGated, Session.SendAnnounce) and withholds it there, as RFC 4271 Section 5.1.3 requires ('A route originated by a BGP speaker SHALL NOT be advertised to a peer using an address of that peer as NEXT_HOP.'). So the antecedent never reaches the wire and the code meets the row vacuously, but no tagged unit carries the row: the untagged TestLinkLocalSecondConditionNeverReachesTheWire (draft_ietf_idr_linklocal_capability_announce_test.go) shows the route withheld while a sibling ::99 route on the same fixture is written, and it is not bound to this id. With no test enforcing the row the honest audit word is unimplemented over the producers named in code; tagging that test with a discrimination record would move the row to met.
